skill.name: excalidraw-diagram-generator
skill.description: Generate Excalidraw diagrams from natural language requests, including flowcharts, mind maps, architecture diagrams, ER diagrams, sequence diagrams, and data flows. The skill produces .excalidraw files and includes optional Python helpers for adding arrows and icon-library elements.
skill.summary: Create editable Excalidraw diagrams from natural language prompts.
skill.author: github

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown formatting, Excalidraw source metadata, template labels, and schema examples. The confirmed issues are limited to Python helper scripts that write caller-selected diagram or library output files; no prompt injection, data exfiltration, or shell execution intent was found.

remediation.issue: Helper scripts write to paths provided on the command line.
remediation.suggestion: Restrict writes to .excalidraw files or approved library directories, and reject unexpected absolute or parent-directory paths.

remediation.issue: Diagram edit helpers can replace existing files during the edit-suffix workflow.
remediation.suggestion: Create timestamped backups before rename or unlink operations, and require explicit confirmation before disabling safe edit mode.

remediation.issue: Documentation includes runnable setup commands for optional icon libraries.
remediation.suggestion: State that assistants should ask the user before running helper scripts or downloading third-party icon libraries.

content.value_statement: Teams often need quick visual diagrams without drawing every shape manually. This skill converts natural language into editable Excalidraw files with structured layouts and reusable templates.
actual_capabilities: Generates .excalidraw files from natural language diagram requests.
Supports flowcharts, mind maps, relationship diagrams, architecture diagrams, ER diagrams, class diagrams, sequence diagrams, and data flows.
Uses bundled templates to keep diagram structure consistent across common diagram types.
Provides layout guidance for spacing, colors, text sizing, arrows, and element counts.
Includes optional Python helpers for adding arrows and icon-library elements to existing diagrams.
Explains how to open generated files in Excalidraw or an editor extension.
limitations: It does not render or visually inspect the final diagram automatically.
Large diagrams may need to be split into smaller files for clarity.
Icon libraries require separate user setup before specialized cloud icons are available.
The helper scripts modify local files when the user chooses to run them.

use_cases.title: Map a Product Workflow
use_cases.description: Create a flowchart that shows user actions, decisions, and handoffs for a product feature.

use_cases.title: Document a System Design
use_cases.description: Generate an architecture diagram with services, data stores, external systems, and labeled connections.

use_cases.title: Plan a Data Model
use_cases.description: Build an ER diagram that shows entities, keys, relationships, and cardinality for a database design.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Flowchart
prompt_templates.scenario: Start with a simple process diagram.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an Excalidraw flowchart for this process: [describe steps]. Include start, decisions, and end states.

prompt_templates.title: Relationship Diagram
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an Excalidraw relationship diagram for [entities]. Label each connection and keep the layout easy to scan.

prompt_templates.title: Architecture Diagram
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an Excalidraw architecture diagram for [system]. Include services, databases, external APIs, data flows, and trust boundaries.

prompt_templates.title: Advanced Icon Diagram
prompt_templates.scenario: Use prepared icon libraries when available.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an Excalidraw cloud architecture diagram using available icon libraries. If icons are missing, create a clear shape-based version.

output_examples.input: Create a flowchart for user registration with email verification and password setup.
output_examples.output: An editable Excalidraw flowchart with a start node, registration steps, verification decision, completion state, and labeled arrows.

output_examples.input: Diagram a blog data model with users, posts, comments, and tags.
output_examples.output: An ER-style Excalidraw diagram with entities, primary keys, foreign keys, and labeled one-to-many relationships.

output_examples.input: Create a sequence diagram for a client calling an API and receiving a response.
output_examples.output: An Excalidraw sequence diagram with actors, lifelines, request messages, processing activation, and return messages.

best_practices: Provide the diagram type, key elements, and desired relationships before generation.
Keep each diagram focused on one process, system level, or data model.
Review generated .excalidraw files in Excalidraw before sharing them.
anti_patterns: Do not request very large diagrams when a focused overview would be clearer.
Do not run helper scripts on files that have not been backed up.
Do not assume third-party icon libraries are installed or licensed for redistribution.

faq.question: What file does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates .excalidraw files that can be opened in Excalidraw or compatible editor extensions.

faq.question: Can it make technical architecture diagrams?
faq.answer: Yes. It can create architecture diagrams with components, data stores, APIs, boundaries, and labeled connections.

faq.question: Does it require internet access?
faq.answer: Basic diagram generation does not require internet access. Optional icon libraries may require the user to download files separately.

faq.question: Can it use AWS or cloud icons?
faq.answer: Yes, when a compatible Excalidraw icon library has been installed and split into the expected local structure.

faq.question: Can I edit the result manually?
faq.answer: Yes. The output is a normal Excalidraw file, so users can adjust shapes, labels, colors, and layout.

faq.question: What should I include in my prompt?
faq.answer: Include the diagram type, important entities or steps, relationships, labels, and any preferred layout constraints.
